analysis: Scope: Linux DMA-BUF cross-vendor transport research plus a bounded Vulkan query-only capability artifact. The artifact leaves import and copy disabled and records UNPROVEN. It does not infer opaque FD legal cross-vendor import or P2P from Vulkan extension advertisements.

Legal versus physical distinction: extension advertisement, handle export/import capability bits, and DEVICE_LOCAL flags are not proof of PCIe peer transactions or driver legal cross-vendor contracts. Legal sharing, physical P2P, host backing, bounce-buffer paths, NUMA, and root-complex behavior must be separated.

Source artifact queries only: Vulkan instance, physical devices, device name, UUID, LUID, PCI bus info when supported, device extensions, memory heaps, memory types, and external buffer/semaphore/fence capabilities for OPAQUE_FD and DMA_BUF when present. It does not allocate, import, export, bind, submit, or copy.

Proof schema required before activation: memory origin, memory location, dedicated allocation receipt, memory type, getfd properties, compatible handle types, imported corresponding resource, ownership transfer, semaphores, fences, cache policy, synchronization, deterministic full payload, independent CPU reference, finite checks, success baseline before corruption control, and per-physical-card residency with real allocations.

Probe matrix: Intel Level Zero peer requires zeDeviceCanAccessPeer success, root/subdevice identity, and ze_peer -q -v -z -i receipts on B60Pro only. CUDA or HIP same-vendor peer requires same-vendor peer enable, residency receipts, deterministic payload, and independent CPU reference. Host staged activation requires host-visible receipts and must never be classified as VRAM P2P. RPC loopback is control-channel only. D3D cross-adapter SYSTEM memory is NOT_APPLICABLE_LINUX. External host unresolved views remain disabled until kernel and driver contracts are proven.

Intel B60Pro Platform Evaluation Guide covers B60Pro only. Do not extrapolate to consumer 8GB Arc or NVIDIA. ACS and IOMMU prerequisites are future read-only measurements only. No BIOS changes are authorized.

NVIDIA CUDA-Vulkan interop primary requires matching same-device UUID. It does not establish an Intel-NVIDIA bridge. Vulkan external memory handle compatibility must be proved per handle type, memory type, dedicated allocation, corresponding resource, ownership, and synchronization.

Linux kernel DMA-BUF documentation describes framework semantics but does not by itself prove vendor-specific acceptance of cross-vendor opaque or DMA-BUF handles into device-local memory. ROCm TransferBench is a measurement source, not a legal ABI proof. Four 8GB discrete target remains NOT_QUALIFIED.

Host shared or imported backing is not VRAM P2P. DEVICE_LOCAL on UMA is not dedicated VRAM. Advertised extensions are not legal resource aliasing or hardware data path proof. Mock contract validator PASS is schema validation only and is not actual GPU qualification.

Existing numerical qualification state remains: actual pinned CPU versus NV/AMD fixed tolerance still fails, max and RMSE values are not improved by this artifact, and tolerance must not be widened. Threads and processes cannot be claimed without real receipts.

Unknown legal ABI and version facts are marked NOT_CHECKED rather than invented. The source leaves import and copy paths disabled. If ROOT later enables probes, each probe must produce immutable receipts and fail closed on missing proof.

Build and use: compile with g++ -std=c++17 vulkan_capability_query.cpp -o vulkan_capability_query -lvulkan, run ./vulkan_capability_query > artifact.json, validate with python3 validator.py < artifact.json. Source is UNTRUSTED until ROOT static compile, actual tests, and admission.
prerequisites: Linux host with Vulkan 1.1 loader and development headers capable of compiling C++17. No driver install, no BIOS changes, no network services, no purchases, no authentication, and no filesystem changes except optional stdout redirection chosen by ROOT.

Compile toolchain: g++ or clang++ plus the Vulkan loader library. Example command: g++ -std=c++17 vulkan_capability_query.cpp -o vulkan_capability_query -lvulkan. The source remains UNTRUSTED until ROOT static compile and admission.

Runtime read-only access to Vulkan physical devices. The query creates only a Vulkan instance and enumerates properties. It does not create a logical device, allocate memory, import handles, or submit work. If enumeration requires elevated permissions, stop and mark NOT_CHECKED.

Future peer or DMA-BUF proofs may collect ACS, IOMMU, BAR, and negotiated link state only as read-only measurements. No BIOS setting changes, no kernel module changes, no privileged sysfs writes, and no driver configuration changes are authorized.

Future Intel Level Zero probes require the supplied level-zero-tests source and the B60Pro guide. Use ze_peer -q -v -z -i only where safely supported and only on B60Pro qualified platforms. Do not extrapolate to consumer Arc or NVIDIA.

Future AMD or NVIDIA same-vendor peer probes require supplied ROCm TransferBench or CUDA primary documentation, actual pinned allocations, finite checks, independent CPU reference, and per-card residency receipts before any PASS.
Python 3 standard library only for the validator. No third-party packages, no network access, and no filesystem mutation. The validator reads JSON from stdin and writes JSON to stdout.
Current host context: NVIDIA 5070 Ti and AMD gfx1036 iGPU present; Intel GPU absent; card SKUs undecided; four 8GB physical discrete target NOT_QUALIFIED. Do not infer target model, price, or speed.
evidence_limits: The source performs no allocation, import, export, copy, peer access, or command submission. Therefore it cannot prove PCIe peer transactions, DMA-BUF cross-vendor legality, or VRAM residency of imported buffers.

Extension presence and external capability bits are advertisements. They are not legal cross-vendor contracts, hardware data path proof, or resource aliasing proof. Compatible handle types do not prove corresponding imported resource semantics.

DEVICE_LOCAL on UMA or host-visible device-local memory is not dedicated discrete VRAM. Host shared or imported backing is not VRAM P2P. Bounce-buffer paths, NUMA behavior, root complex behavior, and PCI topology remain NOT_CHECKED.

Vulkan external memory fd properties that require an actual fd are not queried because no fd is created or imported. getfd properties, import corresponding resource, ownership transfer, cache policy, synchronization compatibility, and external host handle types are NOT_CHECKED.
NVIDIA CUDA-Vulkan interop primary requires matching same-device UUID. It does not provide an Intel-NVIDIA bridge. No Intel-NVIDIA cross-vendor bridge is established by the supplied primaries.

Intel B60Pro Platform Evaluation Guide covers B60Pro only. It is not consumer 8GB Arc proof and not NVIDIA proof. ACS and IOMMU prerequisites are measurements only and are NOT_CHECKED on the current host.
Linux kernel DMA-BUF documentation describes framework semantics but does not prove vendor-specific driver acceptance of cross-vendor opaque or DMA-BUF handles into device-local memory.

ROCm TransferBench is a benchmark and measurement source. It does not by itself establish legal ABI, deterministic payload, independent CPU reference, finite checks, or success baseline before corruption control.

No benchmark, PASS, current price, uniform four-times speed, pool memory, model qualification, or thread/process scaling is claimed. Existing pinned tolerance failures remain and tolerance must not be widened.

Level Zero device API and programming guide are supplied but not exercised by this Vulkan query artifact. zeDeviceCanAccessPeer receipts, root/subdevice identity distinction, and peer physical memory access are NOT_CHECKED.
Mock contract validator PASS only means explicit immutable artifact fields are syntactically and semantically consistent with a disabled import path. It is not actual GPU qualification.

Missing API/version facts, driver-specific cross-device legal contracts, and actual handle/memory type/dedicated/corresponding resource/ownership/synchronization compatibility are NOT_CHECKED rather than invented. Supplied documents were not independently fetched by the model.
